diagnostics.message: :data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this explicitly depends on :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this, but task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.this[0].family already establishes that dependency.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this can launch tasks before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec attaches the execution policy. Referencing the execution role through the task definition does not wait for its policy attachment; order service creation after this attachment so initial tasks have ECR, logging, and configured secret-access permissions.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition can launch tasks before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec attaches the execution policy. Ignoring task_definition changes does not remove the initial deployment's need for ECR, logging, and configured secret-access permissions; order service creation after this attachment.

When additional execution policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.this has no ordering dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec_additional. Tasks may launch before those execution permissions are attached, causing initialization failures for workloads that require them. Wait for these attachments before deploying the service.

When additional execution policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition has no ordering dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec_additional. Its initial tasks may launch before the execution permissions they require are attached. Wait for these attachments before deploying the service.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks. When ECS Exec or custom task-role statements are enabled, tasks and their Exec agent can start before the corresponding permissions are installed. The task-role ARN reference orders role creation, not this inline policy; add ordering on the policy.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks. When ECS Exec or custom task-role statements are enabled, initial tasks and their Exec agent can start before the corresponding permissions are installed. Ignoring task-definition changes does not establish ordering on this inline policy.

When managed task-role policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.this can start the workload before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks attaches its application permissions. A task-role reference does not wait for these attachments. Order deployment after them to avoid startup-time AccessDenied failures.

When managed task-role policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition can start its initial workload before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks attaches its application permissions. A task-role reference does not wait for these attachments; order service deployment after them.

For awsvpc deployments using the module-created security group, :resource.aws_ecs_service.this does not wait for :resource.aws_security_group_rule.this. Terraform removes the group's default allow-all egress rule, so starting tasks before configured egress/ingress rules exist can break image pulls, secret retrieval, or health checks. Order service deployment after these rules.

For awsvpc deployments using the module-created security group, :resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition does not wait for :resource.aws_security_group_rule.this. Security-group existence alone does not ensure configured traffic is allowed; initial tasks can fail initialization or health checks while the separate rules are still being created. Order deployment after the rules.
